meta.audioTone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty, no wink-to-camera jokes. nothing cinematic, nothing anime, nothing triumphant. institutional ambience over music. impact over juice on sfx. vocal grunts are sparse and reluctant — nobody is performing effort for the camera.
meta.boundary: Audio assets only: batched sfx prompts, stage music prompts, impact-IR prompts, sprite-pack layout, and post-process directives. No gameplay rules, runtime selection, or HUD copy.
meta.generationModel: 57 discrete sfx cues are produced by only 15 text-to-audio generations: each 'batch' prompt asks the model to render several related cues back-to-back in one wav file, separated by a fixed silence gap. The post-processor splits the raw wav on silence boundaries, then re-concats everything into the final single-file sprite in spritePack.order. Fewer model calls, higher tonal coherence across related cues, and a single reusable slice pipeline.

spritePack.description: Every sfx cue ships inside one opus-in-webm sprite at assets/audio/sfx/sprite.webm plus a JSON manifest of [startMs, endMs] regions. Cues are generated in batches (see 'batches' below), sliced out of their raw wavs by the post-processor, trimmed/normalized/pad-spliced, then concatenated here in the exact order listed.

_batchProtocol.description: Every batch prompt asks the generator to produce all of its cues in one wav file, back-to-back, with exactly 1000ms of digital silence between each cue and 500ms of silence after the last. The post-processor slices on any silence region >= 700ms below -55 dBFS. cuesOrder must match the order described inside the prompt body or the slicer will mislabel cues.

swipes.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. No wink-to-camera jokes. Nothing cinematic, nothing anime. Render nine distinct weapon-through-air swipes IN ONE WAV, mono, 48 kHz, all in the same dry carpeted-office mic space, each ~0.22-0.40s of actual sound, peaking around -3 dBFS, with EXACTLY 1000ms of digital silence between each, and 500ms of silence after the ninth. Do NOT crossfade. Do NOT ring. No reverb tails. In order:

1) swipe_flail (~240ms) — a heavy rope/chain-whip swipe; brief leather-creak or chain-shiver then a weight passing the mic. Imagine a lanyard with a battery pack on the end, not a medieval flail sample.

2) swipe_maul (~300ms) — a slow, mass-heavy swipe; dominant low-mid air displacement, texture of something that does not want to be moving fast — a loaded duffel or server chassis — ending with a small fabric/strap creak.

3) swipe_blade (~170ms) — a tight, thin swipe; something rigid and flat cutting air cleanly. NOT a shing, NOT a metal ring, NOT a katana. Think stiff plexiglass or a PCB; faintest edge-whistle, no tail.

4) swipe_greatsword (~350ms) — a committed two-handed arc, heavier than swipe_blade, ending with a small settling creak suggestive of rebalancing. No fantasy fanfare, no wind howl.

5) swipe_bat (~220ms) — a dry, short-stroke club swing; a rolled thick bound document swung once, surface friction audible, no resonance. Not a baseball bat whoosh.

6) swipe_club (~190ms) — a stubby one-handed club; blunt object with no aerodynamic shape; air tumbling around it more than cutting.

7) swipe_pike (~260ms) — a long-reach thrust; air parting along a narrow shaft with a small lead-end whistle and a trailing pole resonance that cuts off sharply. Thrust-that-stops, not a javelin throw.

8) swipe_axe (~280ms) — a hinge-weighted swing; head faster than haft, slight mid-arc air-texture wobble, ending with a tiny wood-grain creak from the handle settling. No lumberjack cliche.

9) swipe_nunchucks (~280ms) — TWO rapid air-passes ~90ms apart connected by a faint chain-rattle, then silence. Deliberately unstylish — improvised weapon, not martial-arts showcase.

Remember: 1000ms of pure digital silence between each sound. Mono. No shared reverb.

hits_sama.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. Four weapon-CONTACT sounds for character 'Sama' (archetype: quiet founder with a very expensive weather system; fast setup duelist with polished menace). Render all four IN ONE WAV, mono, 48 kHz, same dry carpeted-office space, each ~0.18-0.26s of actual sound, with EXACTLY 1000ms of digital silence between each and 500ms after the last. No arcade dings, no boss-hit booms, no blood sfx. In order:

1) hit_sama_worldcoin_orb_flail (~190ms) — a coin-shaped metal puck on a tether slaps an opponent; hollow metallic tap (damped, not ringing) followed by ~80ms of tether settling. Feels expensive and slightly absurd.

2) hit_sama_backpack_maul (~210ms) — a heavy padded-weight impact (laptop backpack loaded with hardware hitting a torso); muffled thump up front, a fabric-brush trailing texture. No resonance. Wind-knocked-out energy.

3) hit_sama_gpu_server_blade (~170ms) — a thin rigid edge strikes target; dry plastic-composite crack (PCB snap texture). No metal ring. Something expensive just broke against them.

4) hit_sama_heat_sink_greatsword (~230ms) — a heavy finned-metal slab lands; impact dominated by ribbed-metal rattle (fin vibration) over a dull thud. Short post-impact decay — fins dissipate as high-mid chatter then silence. No sword clang.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

hits_darrius.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. Four weapon-CONTACT sounds for character 'Darrius' (archetype: risk posture with elbows; measured enforcer with long, corrective swings). Render all four IN ONE WAV, mono, 48 kHz, same room, ~0.17-0.28s each, EXACTLY 1000ms silence between, 500ms after last. Bureaucratic humiliation over violence. In order:

1) hit_darrius_rolled_constitution_bat (~190ms) — a thick rolled paper document whacks a target; flat paper-on-body slap, no resonance, faint page-edge flutter at the tail. Bureaucratic and humiliating.

2) hit_darrius_alignment_baton (~170ms) — a rigid short baton strike; one clean tap, slightly higher frequency than bat, very dry. A conductor's baton landing wrong. No rubber-mallet bounce.

3) hit_darrius_red_team_pike (~200ms) — thrust-point lands; sharp front transient (narrow cross-section impacting cloth-over-ribs), brief mid-frequency echo from the shaft, then silence. A point was made, literally.

4) hit_darrius_guardrail_greatsword (~250ms) — a highway-guardrail-profile slab strikes; lower-mid metallic thud with flange/ribbed-steel character, brief industrial shudder as the profile resonates along its length then is gripped back to silence.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

hits_demis.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. Four weapon-CONTACT sounds for character 'Demis' (archetype: polite recursion with unacceptable hands; precise thinker whose weapon geometry looks unfair). Render all four IN ONE WAV, mono, 48 kHz, same room, ~0.17-0.26s each, EXACTLY 1000ms silence between, 500ms after last. Dignified not clangy; unnaturally precise for the fourth. In order:

1) hit_demis_nobel_medal_flail (~190ms) — a heavy gold-weight medallion on a short chain connects; round, short, damped metallic donk (solid puck, not cymbal), medal spins on its chain for ~60ms then held.

2) hit_demis_folded_chess_axe (~210ms) — flat of a folded wood/plastic chessboard swung on a haft; hollow cardboard-over-wood thud with a faint DOUBLE-tap because the two halves hit a hair apart.

3) hit_demis_go_board_maul (~230ms) — a thick slab-wood go board lands with mass; deep wood-on-body thud with subtle grid-plate bounce texture suggesting stones shifting in their bowls but held inside the slab. No obvious 'bonk'.

4) hit_demis_alphafold_blade (~170ms) — an impossibly thin computational blade; impact transient SHORTER than feels physically possible — unnatural snap, almost no spectral content below 500 Hz, brief 3-5 kHz click, then silence. Reads as 'this weapon does not obey the usual rules'.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

hits_mark.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. Four weapon-CONTACT sounds for character 'Mark' (archetype: optimized sincerity with blunt instruments; pressure fighter built from wellness jargon and impact). Render all four IN ONE WAV, mono, 48 kHz, same room, ~0.18-0.23s each, EXACTLY 1000ms silence between, 500ms after last. Comically slightly wrong but not funny. In order:

1) hit_mark_sunscreen_bottle_club (~180ms) — a plastic bottle full of thick lotion bludgeons target; wet-thick slap with a subtle liquid-slosh tail.

2) hit_mark_controller_nunchucks (~190ms) — a hollow-plastic controller-shell, tethered, whips into target; bright plastic crack up front, ~60ms of the second shell swinging in to tap again slightly softer. Cheap and stinging.

3) hit_mark_shareholder_sauce_club (~190ms) — a heavy condiment-bottle club; like sunscreen_bottle_club but thicker, denser, lower slosh register, faint cap-rattle at the tail. Unappetizing.

4) hit_mark_quest_flail (~200ms) — a VR-headset-shaped weight on a short strap swings into target; dense plastic-and-foam impact with a lens-click element at the front (hard plastic rim striking) and brief strap-rustle tail. An expensive gadget has been misused.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

grunts_sama.prompt:
Three short male-voice grunts for character 'Sama' (quiet founder with an expensive weather system; polished menace). Adult male voice, close-mic, dry, mono, 48 kHz, all from the SAME take in the SAME room. No performative fight-shouting — he is annoyed at having to exert himself. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each and 500ms after the last. In order:

1) grunt_sama_effort (~180ms) — a half-exhale 'hhh' with a trace of voiced tone, almost whispered.

2) grunt_sama_hurt (~210ms) — a clipped 'hnngh' or sharp nasal inhale as he absorbs a hit. No scream, no theatrical 'oof'. He is embarrassed to have been hit.

3) grunt_sama_ko (~470ms) — a breath leaving him all at once with a trace of vocal fry, ending in silence. No groan, no last-word. Already thinking about what to say to the board.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

grunts_darrius.prompt:
Three short male-voice grunts for character 'Darrius' (risk posture with elbows; measured enforcer). Adult male voice, chest-voiced, close-mic, dry, mono, 48 kHz, same take, same room. Committed but bored, like a bouncer doing his job. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) grunt_darrius_effort (~180ms) — a low chest-voiced 'huh' on each swing, audibly weight-carrying, not theatrical.

2) grunt_darrius_hurt (~220ms) — a chest-voiced 'nngh', slightly deeper than effort; the grunt is the minimum his body lets him suppress. No yelp.

3) grunt_darrius_ko (~500ms) — a long resigned exhale, heavier vocal fry than sama's. Sounds like he's filing an incident report as he falls.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

grunts_demis.prompt:
Three short male-voice grunts for character 'Demis' (polite recursion with unacceptable hands; precise thinker). Adult male voice, close-mic, dry, mono, 48 kHz, same take, same room. Embarrassed to be making any sound. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) grunt_demis_effort (~170ms) — a short, almost inaudible exhale with a trace of voiced tone, politely muted.

2) grunt_demis_hurt (~200ms) — a tight clipped 'hn' rather than a groan; he is recalculating while being struck.

3) grunt_demis_ko (~470ms) — a quiet collapsing exhale, softer than hurt, trailing into breath-only. A polite apology that has run out of air.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

grunts_mark.prompt:
Three short male-voice grunts for character 'Mark' (optimized sincerity with blunt instruments). Adult male voice, close-mic, dry, mono, 48 kHz, same take, same room. All three sound like they were workshopped — sincere-sounding, not sincere. Slightly too loud for the mic. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) grunt_mark_effort (~180ms) — a mid-register 'hyah'-adjacent effort sound someone clearly thinks sounds natural; effort reads as marketed.

2) grunt_mark_hurt (~220ms) — a slightly performative 'agh' that doesn't quite escape fully, clipped at the end as if he caught himself.

3) grunt_mark_ko (~500ms) — starts as if he's going to say something (small vocal onset), then collapses into unvoiced breath. No closing word.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

movement.prompt:
Tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty. Five movement/body cues, shared across all characters, recorded in the SAME dry carpeted-office space for tonal coherence. Mono, 48 kHz. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) dive_lunge (~280ms) — a short rush of displaced air with a hint of fabric tension (suit jacket shoved forward quickly); mild low-mid whump at start from body weight, thin trailing hiss that ends abruptly. No anime air-slice, no synth dash.

2) spawn_enter (~300ms) — a fighter steps into the arena at round start; soft floor-contact thud (shoe on carpet over concrete) layered with a brief fabric-rustle of jacket settling. Stepping into a meeting, not dropping from the sky.

3) footstep_a (~80ms) — a single footstep; dull shoe-on-industrial-carpet contact, slight scuff texture, no heel-click, no resonance, MARGINALLY higher mid-frequency center than footstep_b.

4) footstep_b (~80ms) — the counterpart; same carpeted-shoe contact with slightly LOWER mid-frequency center and a faint co-occurring heel-scuff. When alternated with footstep_a at ~250ms cadence the pair sounds like one person walking, not a loop.

5) ko_flatline (~470ms) — non-vocal defeat cue meant to layer under a character's ko grunt; one low thud against carpeted concrete followed by a flat unresolved tone decaying in ~400ms, like an HVAC chime that never completes its phrase.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

proof_events.prompt:
Three administrative-sounding objective cues for a proof-bundle game mechanic: the proof appears, gets picked up, and is successfully delivered. Tone: receipt-printer bureaucracy, not arcade chime. Mono, 48 kHz, same dry room, render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) proof_spawn (~280ms) — the proof core appears in the arena; soft magnetic-click up front (hard drive spinning up partway), brief held tone at ~440 Hz decaying over 200ms. Reads as 'a small official object has just become real'. No chime, no sparkle.

2) proof_acquired (~240ms) — a fighter picks up the proof core; crisp mechanical click (hand closing on object) layered with a brief 2-tone rising blip (two semitones around 700 Hz) that feels like a receipt printer confirming something. Understated.

3) proof_delivered (~380ms) — the carrier completed the dwell and scored; two-tone confirmation motif (perfect fourth rising, 220 Hz to 293 Hz) over a faint paper-stamp transient. The receipt printed cleanly. NOT a goal-scored fanfare. Purely administrative.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

proof_carrying_loop.prompt: A 500ms SEAMLESS-LOOPING fragment meant to play quietly and continuously while a fighter is carrying the proof. Mono, 48 kHz. A slow steady low-amplitude hum at ~60 Hz with a faint crystalline shimmer at ~4 kHz pulsing once per 500ms. Barely audible in the mix (-20 dB relative to sfx). The FIRST and LAST 50ms MUST be spectrally and phase identical so the runtime can loop it for the duration of a carry with no audible seam. Render as a SINGLE 500ms wav (no silence before or after — the whole wav is the loop). Since this entry is its own batch with a single cue, no inter-cue silence applies.

goal_timer.prompt:
Four austere objective-timer cues for a demand-node delivery target with a countdown timer. Tone: institutional, not arcade. All four share a consistent fluorescent-lit room sound. Mono, 48 kHz. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) goal_spawn (~260ms) — a demand node has appeared; low pulse (~80 Hz) rises and holds for 200ms then cuts off. A deadline is now running. No chime, no sparkle.

2) goal_tick (~70ms) — non-urgent per-second tick while timer > 3 seconds; one dry clock-escapement click with a trace of desk resonance. Low-volume; must tile once per second without fatigue.

3) goal_urgent_tick (~110ms) — urgent per-second tick when timer ≤ 3 seconds; a flat, slightly harsh fluorescent-ballast alarm blip around 1 kHz, followed by 40ms of silence. Unmistakable against goal_tick without being melodramatic. Institutional, not arcade.

4) goal_expire (~350ms) — timer reached zero without a delivery; one short descending unresolved tone (400 Hz down to 280 Hz over ~120ms) followed by room tone. The window closed, nobody got credit. No buzzer, no failure stinger.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono.

match_flow.prompt:
Four match/round transition cues. Shared palette: a fluorescent-lit conference phone and the room it sits in. Tone: meetings starting and ending, not fights starting and ending. Mono with narrow-stereo allowed for round_taken only, 48 kHz. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) match_start (~350ms) — a double-beep from the conference phone (both beeps in ~350ms total), steady pitch, no swell, followed by 100ms of room tone. A meeting is starting, not a fight.

2) round_start (~260ms) — a single short phone-beep (~200ms steady pitch) followed by 60ms of room tone. Quieter than match_start; rounds happen more often.

3) round_end (~300ms) — a low held tone that decays without resolution (~260 Hz for 240ms, 60ms silence). Sounds like the call-in line has dropped. No stinger. Fires on timeout paths only.

4) round_taken (~480ms) — THE stinger when a fighter takes the round by reaching POINTS_TO_WIN_ROUND deliveries; a first percussive paper-stamp transient (a receipt getting stamped 'APPROVED') followed ~120ms later by a brief held tone at ~392 Hz (G4) decaying over 300ms. Unresolved — it's a round, not the match — but unmistakably a WIN event. More shape than round_end. No chord, no fanfare, no rising interval, no crowd. Institutional satisfaction: a line item was closed.

1000ms pure silence between. Mono (narrow stereo acceptable for cue 4).

match_end.prompt:
Three match-ending cues. Tone: a meeting concluding, not a championship being decided. Mono except win_applause which may be narrow stereo. 48 kHz. Render IN ONE WAV with EXACTLY 1000ms of silence between each, 500ms after last. In order:

1) match_end_win (~450ms) — a single low sustained unresolved tone (~450ms) followed by a short exhale of room tone. No fanfare, no chord resolution, no rising interval. Sounds more like the lights have been turned off than like a victory. win_applause fires AFTER this cue, not simultaneously.

2) match_end_draw (~500ms) — identical texture to match_end_win but two tones detuned a quarter-tone apart, canceling into a faint beat. Expresses 'nothing was decided' rather than 'both competed well'.

3) win_applause (~2200ms) — audience reaction after a match win, but NOT a stadium crowd. Thin small-room applause from a handful of people (4-8 claps audible) in a carpeted conference space, slightly out of sync, a little too sparse to feel like a full room. Add one late clap at ~1.9s from the back of the room. No cheers, no whistles, no vocal whoops. Emotional read: 'polite obligation' more than 'celebration'. Narrow stereo.

1000ms pure silence between. See per-cue channel notes.

cold_aisle_chapel.prompt: a 48-second seamless ambient loop for a server room rendered as a chapel. constant low blower drone around 55-80 Hz, a steady fluorescent ballast hum near 120 Hz that never varies, faint intermittent hard-drive chatter as micro-percussive texture (not rhythmic). no melody. no chord progression. no drums. no pad swells. stereo field narrow and cold. the first 500ms and last 500ms must share identical spectral content so the loop seam is inaudible; do not fade in or out, and do not place a transient near either boundary. mixed with substantial air (~-22 LUFS).

fiduciary_basement.prompt: a 56-second seamless ambient loop for a basement-level corporate boardroom. foundation is an HVAC rumble around 40-60 Hz, a slow breathing low-frequency oscillation (one cycle every ~8 seconds) like a compressor cycling. no melody, no chord progression, no drums. add very sparse, slightly detuned long-held tones (cello or sine, 2-3 per loop, each 6-10 seconds, always dissonant to the last one by a minor second or tritone). stereo width narrow. boundaries: first 750ms matches last 750ms spectrally and phase-continuously; no transient near either end. target ~-22 LUFS.

demo_day_afterparty.prompt: a 64-second seamless loop for a stage whose art depicts the hour after a tech conference ends. the sound is muffled dance music bleeding through a closed door from two rooms away — heavily low-pass filtered (cutoff ~400 Hz), side-chained slightly so a ghost of the kick pattern is detectable but never fully audible. tempo around 122 BPM so it tiles the 64s window in an integer number of bars. over the bleed, add faint HVAC drone and distant intermittent voice murmurs (no intelligible words). feels like 'the party is ending and you are not in the room where it happened'. seam boundaries identical; integer bar count so the kick pulse is phase-continuous across the seam. target ~-22 LUFS.

stageImpactReverb.description: Per-stage impulse response used by a ConvolverNode on the impact bus at runtime. Only hit_* cues are routed through this bus; swipes, grunts, footsteps, and match-flow cues stay dry. Bus is wet/dry-mixed per stage; ambient music and objective cues bypass it entirely. IRs are short (<=800ms) and stored alongside the stage's music file. Crossfade the ConvolverNode's buffer over 1.5s when the stage changes (mirrors the music crossfade duration).

cold_aisle_chapel.prompt: a short impulse response capturing the reflective character of a cold data-center aisle — tall metal rack walls, concrete floor under raised tile, minimal absorbers. starts with a sharp direct pulse at t=0, followed by dense early reflections from 8-25ms (narrow, hard, high-frequency-heavy — the racks reflect cleanly above 2 kHz), then a short bright tail decaying over ~350ms with a slight fluorescent-tuned resonance around 120 Hz. mono-in/stereo-out acceptable but narrow. NOT a cathedral reverb, NOT a warm hall. cold, reflective, surgical. the IR should make a hit sfx feel like it was struck inside a steel cage, not a concert venue.

fiduciary_basement.prompt: a short impulse response capturing a basement-level executive boardroom: low ceiling, heavy carpet, wood paneling, long table absorbing mids. sharp direct pulse at t=0, sparse early reflections 15-40ms (diffuse, mid-heavy, dampened above 4 kHz by the carpet), then a short dry tail decaying over ~450ms with absorbed high end and a faint wood-panel resonance around 250 Hz. the IR should make a hit feel like it happened under fluorescent lights with witnesses who did not react. not plush, not cinematic; officially muffled.

demo_day_afterparty.prompt: a short impulse response capturing an empty post-conference demo-day hall — high ceiling, scattered partition walls, flooring half-carpet half-concrete, lingering low-frequency haze from PA gear being powered down. direct pulse at t=0, moderately dense early reflections 10-60ms with slight low-mid emphasis (the empty hall rings just a little), a soft diffuse tail decaying over ~580ms that loses its high end gracefully but holds a faint ~80 Hz body. the IR should make a hit feel like it echoed faintly through a hall that used to be full an hour ago.

triggerMap.swipe_{class}: fire when any fighter.swipeT transitions 0 -> positive in interpolated frame output. resolve {class} from fighter.loadout.weaponId -> weapon.class (flail/maul/blade/greatsword/bat/club/pike/axe/nunchucks). fallback: swipe_blade.
triggerMap.hit_{char}_{weaponId}: fire when opp.hp decreases between consecutive frames. resolve {char} from the attacker's characterId and {weaponId} from their loadout. do NOT fire on swipeT alone — swings can miss. if manifest lookup fails, fall back to any hit_{char}_* (pick heaviest class).
triggerMap.grunt_{char}_effort: fire with the swipe cue on the attacker's edge. per-character throttle: suppress if same character emitted effort in the last 400ms.
triggerMap.grunt_{char}_hurt: fire with the hit cue on the victim's edge. same 400ms throttle.
triggerMap.grunt_{char}_ko: fire with ko_flatline on fighter.dead false -> true. ko_flatline is the non-vocal layer; the per-character grunt is the vocal layer. play both simultaneously.
triggerMap.spawn_enter: fire once per fighter at round start. stagger per-fighter firings by 80ms.
triggerMap.footstep_a / footstep_b: per-fighter step-phase timer driven by horizontal velocity while grounded. alternate A/B each step. suppress during dead/dive/swipe/hit-stun. target ~4 steps/sec at top walk speed. mix -18 dB vs hits.
triggerMap.round_taken: fire when a fighter's delivery count reaches POINTS_TO_WIN_ROUND. suppresses round_end on the same transition.
triggerMap.round_end: fire on round-advance that is NOT a decisive delivery win (timer expiry, etc.). round_taken takes precedence.
triggerMap.proof_spawn: fire when the proof core spawns into the arena.
triggerMap.proof_acquired: fire when FighterTelemetry transitions not-carrying -> carrying.
triggerMap.proof_carrying_loop_fragment: start looping on proof_acquired; stop on proof_delivered OR carrier death. played as a quiet bed.
triggerMap.goal_spawn: fire when a demand node appears.
triggerMap.goal_tick: fire once per second while goal timer is running AND timer > 3s.
triggerMap.goal_urgent_tick: fire once per second while goal timer is running AND timer <= 3s. suppresses goal_tick during the urgent window.
triggerMap.goal_expire: fire when goal timer reaches 0 without a delivery.
triggerMap.round_start: fire at the start of rounds 2+ (not round 1 — match_start covers that).
triggerMap.win_applause: schedule ~250ms after match_end_win's onset. never on draw.

integrationNotes.primePlaybackSuppression: After primePlayback() jumps to the newest frame on (re)mount or after trimPlaybackToLiveWindow(), suppress ALL edge-detection-based cues for the first rendered frame — otherwise buffered state differences fire every cue at once. Exception: match_start/matchEnd are ws-driven and safe.
integrationNotes.impactBusRouting: hit_* cues are the ONLY cues routed through the stage's ConvolverNode. Everything else connects directly to master. On stage change, crossfade the ConvolverNode's buffer over 1.5s (matches music crossfade). If IR not loaded yet at the moment of a hit, route dry for that frame.

playback.singleFile: All sfx ship as one file: assets/audio/sfx/sprite.webm + manifest. No per-cue network I/O. Music tracks are separate per stage. Impact IRs are separate per stage.
playback.spriteSeeking: Decode sprite.webm once into a single AudioBuffer at first user gesture. Trigger via AudioBufferSourceNode.start(when, offsetSec, durationSec). Do not use HTMLAudioElement for the sprite.
playback.voices: 8-voice pool for one-shots; steal oldest non-vocal on exhaustion (never steal grunts). proof_carrying_loop_fragment owns a long-lived node. footstep_a/b share a separate 2-voice pool.
playback.music: one AudioBufferSourceNode per stage, loop=true, loopStart=0, loopEnd=buffer.duration. crossfade on stage change over 1.5s.
playback.masterToggle: localStorage 'm3t4:audio:on', default false. Toggle lives in the Live sidebar. When off, master GainNode.gain = 0 (do not tear down). First toggle-on performs the one-time decode.
playback.firstGesture: AudioContext starts on first toggle-on click, not on page mount.

batchSfxPipeline: for each entry in 'batches': read raw generation from generations/raw/audio/batches/<batchId>.wav
detect silence regions: contiguous samples where abs-peak stays below batches._batchProtocol.sliceFloorDbfs (-55 dBFS) for >= 700ms
the expected slice count is batches[batchId].cuesOrder.length; if detected count differs, REJECT the batch and log — do not guess
split wav at the midpoint of each detected silence region; label each slice in left-to-right order with cuesOrder[i]

for each resulting per-cue clip: trim leading silence below -50 dBFS, hard-cut or zero-pad to sfx[cue].durationSec, loudness-normalize to meta.format.targetLUFS.sfx, peak-limit to meta.format.peakCeilingDb, append spritePack.padTrailingMs of digital silence
assemble final sprite by reading spritePack.order and concatenating the post-processed clips in that exact order
encode sprite to opus @ 96 kbps in webm
emit manifest { [id]: [startMs, endMs] } using pre-padding end offsets
musicPipeline: for each stageMusic entry: read from generations/raw/audio/stages/<stageId>/<variant>/music.wav
verify loop seam: spectral centroid of first and last 500ms match within 3%; RMS within 1 dB; for demoday also verify integer bar count at declared tempo
if seam verification fails, REJECT and log — never silently crossfade
encode opus @ 128 kbps stereo in webm
write to the entry's 'out' path under client/
impactIrPipeline: for each stageImpactReverb.stages entry: read from generations/raw/audio/stages/<stageId>/<variant>/impact_ir.wav
enforce maxTailMs (800ms) — hard-cut any tail beyond
ensure t=0 is the direct pulse (trim leading silence below -60 dBFS)
normalize IR energy to unit gain; wetSendDb is the only runtime loudness control
encode opus @ 96 kbps in webm at declared channel count
